accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Pabna Movement occurred in East Bengal during 1873–76. The Deccan Riots were centred in Poona-Ahmednagar, Bardoli was in Gujarat, and Tebhaga was in Bengal.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure region-year pair and eliminate the swapped locations.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following peasant movements in chronological order:
A. Pabna Movement
B. Champaran Movement
C. Deccan Riots
D. Indigo Revolt
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Indigo Revolt (1859–60), Deccan Riots (1875), Pabna Movement (1873–76), and Champaran Movement (1917). Since the periods of Pabna and Deccan overlap in the table, the sequence conventionally places the beginning of Pabna before the 1875 Deccan Riots; hence the precise chronological order is D, A, C, B.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then split the close middle dates.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Agrarian League associated with the Pabna Movement was led by which of the following?
o: Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
accepted.x: Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal led the Agrarian League connected with the Pabna Movement.
accepted.tq: Test the leader-organisation association directly; nearby movements provide the distractors.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Pabna Movement is correct?
o: It was a violent revolt against moneylenders in the Deccan.
It was a legal and peaceful movement against rent increases by zamindars.
It was a campaign against revenue enhancement in Gujarat.
It was a sharecroppers' movement for two-thirds of the crop in Bengal.
accepted.x: The Pabna Movement was a legal and peaceful agrarian movement against rent increases imposed by zamindars. It contributed to the enactment of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar peasant movements by identifying the target and method.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Pabna Movement contributed to the enactment of which legislation?
accepted.x: The legal and peaceful Pabna agitation against zamindari rent increases helped lead to the Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885.
accepted.tq: Use the movement-legislation link rather than confusing it with relief laws of other regions.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Telangana armed struggle occurred in Hyderabad State. Malabar was the region of the Moplah Movement; Kheda was in Gujarat, Bijolia in Mewar, and the Sanyasi Revolt in Bengal.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly shifted regional label among otherwise familiar pairings.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sanyasi Revolt was associated with which of the following circumstances?
o: The introduction of the Limitation Law of 1859
The demand for two-thirds of the crop by bargadars
The famine of 1770 and restrictions on pilgrimages
accepted.x: The Sanyasi Revolt in Bengal during 1763–1800 was linked with the aftermath of the 1770 famine and restrictions imposed on pilgrimages.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive cause rather than the region alone.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the Bijolia Movement?
o: Mohanlal Pandya and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
Ali Musliyar and Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji
accepted.x: The Bijolia Movement in Mewar was associated with Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik.
accepted.tq: Test the movement-leader pair while using leaders from neighbouring movements as traps.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the All India Kisan Sabha:
1. It functioned as the peasant wing of the Congress.
2. It demanded the abolition of zamindari.
3. It demanded cancellation of peasant debts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The All India Kisan Sabha worked as the peasant wing of the Congress and demanded both abolition of zamindari and cancellation of debts.
accepted.tq: Check whether all three policy objectives belong to the same organisation.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded at which Congress session?
accepted.x: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in April 1936 at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-session-year combination and reject nearby Congress session years.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The journal Hunkar was associated with which of the following leaders?
accepted.x: Hunkar was the paper published by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
accepted.tq: Match the publication with its correct peasant leader.
accepted.sec: All India Kisan Sabha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the immediate target of the Deccan Riots of 1875?
accepted.x: The peasants attacked moneylenders, particularly outsiders from Gujarat and Marwar, who had seized peasant land through debt-related processes.
accepted.tq: Identify the actual target instead of accepting a broad but incomplete cause.
accepted.sec: Deccan Riots - target and relief Act  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the Deccan Riots, the peasants primarily attacked moneylenders’ houses and burned which of the following?
accepted.x: The rioters attacked the houses of moneylenders and burned their debt bonds, which represented the oppressive credit relationships.
accepted.tq: Test the specific action associated with the revolt rather than its general grievance.
accepted.sec: Deccan Riots - target and relief Act  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act was enacted in response to the Deccan agrarian disturbances in which year?
accepted.x: The Government responded to the Deccan disturbances by enacting the Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act in 1879.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the disturbance from the year of the relief legislation.
accepted.sec: Deccan Riots - target and relief Act  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which combination correctly describes the Deccan agrarian context?
o: Ryotwari system, Limitation Law of 1859 and land seizure by moneylenders
Tinkathia system, zamindari rent enhancement and forced indigo cultivation
Taluqdari system, begar and crop storage in peasant godowns
Mahalwari system, railway construction and plantation labour
accepted.x: The Deccan Riots occurred in a ryotwari context; the Limitation Law of 1859 facilitated debt-related land seizure by moneylenders.
accepted.tq: Combine the system, law and causal relationship instead of relying on the revolt’s name alone.
accepted.sec: Deccan Riots - target and relief Act  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The main grievances of the Oudh Kisan Sabha were directed against which practices of the taluqdars?
accepted.x: The Oudh Kisan Sabha addressed rent increases and begar, or forced labour, imposed by taluqdars.
accepted.tq: Link the regional Kisan Sabha with its specific agrarian grievances.
accepted.sec: Kisan Sabhas in UP and Oudh; Eka vs Bardoli  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly differentiates the Eka Movement from the Bardoli Satyagraha?
o: Eka was led by Patel in Gujarat, whereas Bardoli was led by Madari Pasi in Oudh.
Eka was under Madari Pasi and became violent, whereas Bardoli was a disciplined non-violent Congress campaign led by Patel.
Both movements were controlled directly by the Congress and remained non-violent.
Both movements were directed against moneylenders in the Deccan.
accepted.x: The Eka Movement of 1921–22 operated in Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur under Madari Pasi, became violent and remained outside Congress control. Bardoli was a disciplined, non-violent Congress campaign led by Patel.
accepted.tq: Use the leadership, region and method together to separate two easily confused movements.
accepted.sec: Kisan Sabhas in UP and Oudh; Eka vs Bardoli  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Eka Movement was mainly associated with which geographical area?
accepted.x: The Eka Movement of 1921–22 was concentrated in the Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur areas of Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the regional cluster rather than confusing it with the similarly named Oudh Kisan Sabha.
accepted.sec: Kisan Sabhas in UP and Oudh; Eka vs Bardoli  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Tebhaga Movement, consider the following statements:
1. It took place in Bengal during 1946–47.
2. It was led by the All India Kisan Sabha and the Communist Party of India.
3. Bargadars demanded that their crop share be increased from one-half to two-thirds.
4. The crop was to be stored in the bargadars’ own godowns.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the Tebhaga Movement in Bengal. Bargadars demanded two-thirds of the crop and wanted it stored in their own godowns.
accepted.tq: Verify the province, leadership, numerical demand and operational detail together.
accepted.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

accepted.s: The term ‘Tebhaga’ referred to the demand of sharecroppers for:
o: One-half of the crop stored in the landlord’s godown
Two-thirds of the crop instead of one-half
One-third of the crop instead of one-half
The entire crop without payment of rent
accepted.x: The bargadars demanded two-thirds of the produce, reducing the landlord’s share from one-half to one-third, with storage in their own godowns.
accepted.tq: Watch the reversed-share trap: the demand concerns the bargadar’s share, not the landlord’s share.
accepted.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which legislation is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga Movement?
accepted.x: The Bargadari Act of 1950 is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga struggle.
accepted.tq: Match the movement with its later legislative outcome while rejecting earlier regional laws.
accepted.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the limited short-run success of the Tebhaga Movement?
o: A government ban before the movement began and a famine in Gujarat
The transfer of the movement from Bengal to Hyderabad
Limited spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift
Complete support from all zamindars and the absence of peasant participation
accepted.x: The movement’s short-run success was limited by its restricted spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired outcome factors rather than confusing them with causes of other movements.
accepted.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the broad historical transition in Indian peasant movements?
o: From sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders to Gandhian satyagraha and then organised Kisan Sabhas
From organised Kisan Sabhas to sporadic revolts and then to plantation movements
From tribal movements to exclusive urban labour movements
From revolutionary violence directly to constitutional reforms without mass participation
accepted.x: Before 1917, peasant movements were often sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders; they later developed into Gandhian satyagraha and organised Kisan Sabhas in the 1930s.
accepted.tq: Recognise the chronological sequence of changing forms of agrarian mobilisation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to peasant movements in Gujarat?
o: Bardoli — Baba Ramchandra and Madari Pasi
Kheda — Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Bardoli — Ali Musliyar and Kunjahammad Haji
accepted.x: Kheda in Gujarat was associated with Patel and Mohanlal Pandya. The other pairs combine leaders from Uttar Pradesh, Bengal and Malabar movements.
accepted.tq: Use the region first, then verify the associated leaders.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Telangana peasant movement of 1946–51 was associated with which combination?
o: Hyderabad, the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha
Bengal, the Indian National Congress and the Agrarian League
Gujarat, the Congress Socialist Party and the All India Trade Union Congress
Mewar, the Muslim League and the Oudh Kisan Sabha
accepted.x: The Telangana armed struggle occurred in Hyderabad during 1946–51 and was associated with the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Combine the region, period and organisations to avoid confusing Telangana with Tebhaga.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The anti-zamindari struggles in Andhra Pradesh mentioned in connection with land reform included which of the following?
accepted.x: The Nellore and Munagala anti-zamindari struggles are highlighted as important Andhra-related agrarian movements. Land reform demands also contributed to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill of 1947.
accepted.tq: Identify the Andhra-specific locations rather than selecting nationally prominent movement centres.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill was introduced in which year in the context of land reform demands?
accepted.x: Land reform demands associated with agrarian struggles led to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill in 1947.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the bill’s year from the years of the Kisan Sabha and Bargadari legislation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Moplah Movement is correct?
o: It occurred in Maharashtra in 1875 and targeted moneylenders from Gujarat and Marwar.
It occurred in Bengal in 1946 and was led by bargadars demanding two-thirds of the crop.
It occurred in Gujarat in 1928 as a non-violent Congress campaign against revenue enhancement.
It occurred in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants against landlords and the British.
accepted.x: The Moplah Movement took place in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants in conflict with landlords and the British.
accepted.tq: Separate Moplah from Tebhaga, Deccan and Bardoli through region, year and target.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of leaders was associated with the Moplah Movement?
o: Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
accepted.x: Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar were associated with the Moplah Movement in Malabar.
accepted.tq: Match the movement with its distinctive leadership rather than its general social base.
accepted.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]
